ARCHITECTURE: manager.ts completely rewritten as deterministic dedup — no Claude/Gemini calls.

PATTERN: After curation stores memories, run synchronous dedup pass on new memory IDs.

RULE 1 — Domain+Feature+Headline dedup:
  Find active memories with same domain+feature+>80% headline word overlap → supersede older one
  Sets: status:'superseded', superseded_by:<new_id> on the old memory

RULE 2 — State dedup:
  context_type:'state' for same project — keep newest, supersede all older
  Always-current: state memories represent 'now', not history

RULE 3 — Tag linking:
  3+ shared semantic_tags between memories → add to related_to array on both
  Uses store.updateMemory with related_to field

API: manage(store: MemoryStore, projectId: string, newMemoryIds: string[]): Promise<ManagementResult>
  Returns: { superseded: string[], linked: string[][], errors: string[] }

WHY: LLM-based manager had failure modes (API errors, hallucinations, slow). Deterministic is fast, always works, predictable.

REJECTED: Kept LLM for dedup (too slow, unreliable). Gemini CLI (external dependency, flaky).
